justification.mechanism: Higher and more stable yields, irrigation of gardens and higher-value crops from stored water, and better fodder and livestock raise household income and food security; beneficiaries shift from staples to vegetables, and a quasi-experimental study cited in a review found soil and water conservation raised net rice profit in Ghana by a significant 16 per cent [ev_household_income_veno12_2, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_economic_return_mala24_1]. WOCAT compilers describe the same pathway: planting pits in Uganda keep banana stands fruiting through drought and raise harvests for sale, ripper tillage in Zambia gives better tolerance to dry spells at lower tillage cost, farm ponds in Cambodia supply irrigation during drought, and contour stone bunds in Bhutan enlarge the cultivable area for diverse crops [ev_food_security_wocat_1587_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1587_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1139_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1139_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_risk_of_production_failure]. WOCAT compilers' own benefit-versus-cost ratings point the same way, judging the long-term returns on both establishment and maintenance positive or very positive on nearly every sheet. In Kenya, farmers living near sand dams saw average income rise by 60% as more water in dry periods raised farm yields [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. An Ethiopian synthesis reports positive net present values of 3486.2 Birr per hectare for stone bunds, 2794.0 for bench terraces and 5283.4 for level fanya juu [ev_economic_return_adim16_1, ev_economic_return_adim16_2, ev_economic_return_adim16_3]; In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers earned a maize gross margin of 473.36 USD per hectare against 70.60 on conventional plots in the low-rainfall budget, with 866.84 against 357.16 for experienced farmers in high rainfall [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2]; and ground cover raised the odds of a Malawian plot meeting the household maize requirement in the El Niño season, and planting basins sharply raised those odds in a good Kenyan season [ev_food_security_boil19_1, ev_food_security_boil19_2]. Reviews add that rainwater-harvesting ponds brought statistically significant gains in household income and food security in Burkina Faso, water storage gave Ethiopian smallholders greater income security, harvested water used with precision irrigation in Ethiopia reached a net water value of up to 1.53 USD per cubic metre, and benefit-cost ratios of up to 3.38 with payback periods of 6.8 to 12 years; Indian farms with a farm pond reported net returns of 857 USD per hectare against 586 without [ev_household_income_silv26_1, ev_household_income_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_silv26_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. Modelled bench-terrace gains in Peru could raise per capita incomes by up to 15%, and a review tabulates significantly increased food security and incomes from check dams and infiltration pits in Malawi [ev_household_income_wei16_1, ev_food_security_ngur26_1]. Against the fertilised conventional arm in the same Zimbabwe budget the first-year margin was 473.36 against 48.19 US dollars per hectare [ev_economic_return_mazv09_3]. In Zimbabwe's El Niño season, no-till with a residue mulch returned a cost-benefit ratio of 1.39 against 1.05 for conventional tillage [ev_economic_return_mash25h1_3]. A review cites reduced tillage with residue maintained giving the highest net benefit and marginal rate of return on teff [ev_economic_return_tade23h1_4]. On crusted degraded soil in Burkina Faso, 1-m half-moons with compost were profitable at 377 275 FCFA per hectare after the investment [ev_economic_return_zour25h1_3]. Higher yields are cited as improving household food security in Burkina Faso, especially on farms that apply manure or some kind of soil and water conservation on over half their plots [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5]. A review cites soil and water conservation measures, including level bunds and fanya juu terraces, boosting farmer income by increasing soil fertility, yield and water [ev_household_income_tade23h1_1]. In Zambia, crop budgets for hand-hoe conservation-farming basins give returns per hectare 70 percent higher than conventional hand hoe cultivation and 150 percent higher than conventional plowing for cotton, and returns to land and to peak-season labor 60 to 90 percent higher than hand hoe tillage for maize [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_hagg03_7, ev_economic_return_hagg03_8]. In Brazil, an Embrapa survey of some communities found small-farm incomes rose by about half a minimum wage per month after the second filling of the barraginhas, and adopters rated food security as the technology's largest impact [ev_household_income_mira19_1, ev_food_security_mira19_2].
justification.conditionality: The roll-up states conflicting evidence because the sub-practice rows disagree: the runoff-catchment, micro-catchment, spate and terracing rows each lean positive, while the in-field and cross-family rows are each split between gains and losses. What pulls the in-field side apart is how the gain is valued and against what. Crop budgets built on bundled input packages, and the practitioner ratings, put basins well ahead [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_hagg03_8, ev_economic_return_mazv09_1]; but a Zimbabwe household panel that values predicted yields with inputs held constant finds conservation agriculture (mostly planting basins, with residue mulch and rotation on some plots) generates less revenue than traditional cultivation over a large portion of the rainfall distribution, and its revenue comes out ahead only when rainfall is far from the mean [ev_economic_return_mich19_8]. The other losses are season- or practice-specific: banking in Malawi's El Nino season, tied ridging in a Kenyan drought season, and 30-cm zaï on a Burkina Faso trial [ev_food_security_boil19_3, ev_economic_return_ndun23_1, ev_economic_return_zour25h1_4]. In the cross-family row, gains from bundled programmes and cistern income sit against costs exceeding gains: single soil and water conservation measures not covering their annual costs in Burkina Faso, negative net present values for graded Ethiopian structures, a Brazilian production-cistern benefit-cost ratio far below break-even, and Niger families with soil and water conservation still in deficit in low-rainfall years [ev_economic_return_zoug14_3, ev_economic_return_adim16_4, ev_economic_return_casag22_9, ev_food_security_kabo04_1]; there farm size, how household labour is costed, where structures are built and the rainfall year separate the sides. Most pooled units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT technology sheets, including compilers' benefit-versus-cost judgements rather than measured returns, and much of the literature comes from bundled watershed programmes and lender completion or appraisal reports, so measured household effects are a minority. Independent evaluations are more cautious: no significant effect on food security or total income in Ethiopian programmes, terraces reducing net crop income, a Brazilian production-cistern programme with a benefit-cost ratio far below break-even, single SWC measures not covering their annual costs, and sand dams likely not cost-efficient [ev_food_security_abate21_4, ev_food_security_arega24_1, ev_household_income_mala24_1, ev_economic_return_casag22_9, ev_economic_return_zoug14_3, ev_economic_return_ritc21_1]. Compilers also rate check-dam land in China as raising the risk of production failure in extreme wet years and record no change on several sheets, including a subsistence farm pond in India; Kenyan sand dams sit inside a wider food-security programme, and food security, income and returns are all proxies for poverty [ev_food_security_wocat_1455_2011_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1474_2011_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1537_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Short-term returns on establishment are rated slightly to very negative on sheets from Tunisia, China, Rwanda, Yemen, Cabo Verde, Nicaragua, Jordan, Uzbekistan and Somalia, reflecting up-front costs that are only recovered over time. The Kenyan sand-dam income rise compares a small sample of households with a control catchment [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. New evidence adds further limits: the same synthesis reports negative net present values for graded fanya juu (−148 Birr per hectare) and graded soil bunds (−708 Birr per hectare), possibly because off-site benefits were left out [ev_economic_return_adim16_4]; cost savings from conservation agriculture are usually small for smallholders; and in a Kenyan drought season net benefits were higher without tied ridging [ev_economic_return_corb20_1, ev_economic_return_ndun23_1]. The Zimbabwe planting-basin margins include manure and fertiliser and the high-rainfall figure is a sensitivity scenario, the Indian pond returns are cross-sectional from a preprint survey confounded by farm size and assets, the reviewed income and water-value figures are secondary citations at their upper end, and the Peruvian income gain is modelled [ev_economic_return_mazv09_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_household_income_wei16_1]. In Malawi's El Nino season banking lowered the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement from 0.19 to 0.054, so a mis-timed in-field practice can cut food security rather than raise it [ev_food_security_boil19_3]. 30-cm zaï on the same Burkina Faso trial ran at a loss (−98 624 FCFA per hectare), smaller than the direct-seeding loss, and the investment counted is the experiment's own cost [ev_economic_return_zour25h1_4]. The Zimbabwe ratio is a single drought-season budget with the mulch bundled with no-till [ev_economic_return_mash25h1_3]. The teff returns are cited second-hand [ev_economic_return_tade23h1_4]. The Burkina Faso food-security statement is cited and does not separate manure from soil and water conservation [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5]. The Ethiopian income claim is cited from a study that the citing review itself describes as methodologically weak [ev_household_income_tade23h1_1]. The Zambian returns are crop budgets with output estimated from regression coefficients, bundled with early planting and purchased inputs (hybrid seed and fertiliser for maize), and the authors say early-planting gains dominate the maize results [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_hagg03_8]. The Zimbabwe panel figure is gross revenue at later market prices with labour and non-market inputs unvalued, so it is neither a profit nor a poverty measure [ev_economic_return_mich19_8]. The barraginha income and food-security findings are Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, from an informal survey and adopter ratings with no normal-year reference [ev_household_income_mira19_1, ev_food_security_mira19_2].

effect_mechanism: Household income and returns from soil and water conservation and water harvesting have been found to rise, to stay flat and to fall. Gains run through higher yields, irrigation and diversification: a quasi-experimental study found soil and water conservation raised net rice profit in Ghana by a significant 16 per cent [ev_economic_return_mala24_1]; Brazil's production-cistern programme raised family income by about 4.6%, nearly 11% when the top of the income distribution is excluded, with larger effects on farms of 0 to 10 ha [ev_household_income_casag22_1, ev_household_income_casag22_2, ev_household_income_casag22_5]; a review of 311 Indian watershed case studies found a modest mean benefit-cost ratio of 2.14 and an internal rate of return of 22 percent [ev_economic_return_josh05_1, ev_economic_return_josh05_2]; Mauritanian dikes returned a financial IRR of 24% [ev_economic_return_mrt14_4]; and programme evaluations report income gains of 54% in Karnataka and 58% on the Loess Plateau over control areas [ev_household_income_iegind11_2, ev_household_income_iegchn07_6]. Losses and shortfalls come from costs exceeding gains: in Burkina Faso the yield increase did not cover the annual costs of single SWC measures [ev_economic_return_zoug14_3]; Ethiopian graded fanya juu and graded soil bunds had negative net present values of −148 and −708 ETB per hectare [ev_economic_return_adim16_4]; the Brazilian cistern programme's benefit-cost ratio over its evaluation window was 0.0858 [ev_economic_return_casag22_9]; and in Niger, families with SWC produced a 70 percent surplus in good rainfall years but a 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1].
conditionality: What separates the sides, where the evidence says it: farm size and income, since the Brazilian income effect was positive on small farms but negative on farms larger than 10 ha [ev_household_income_casag22_5, ev_household_income_casag22_6]; labour costing and the size of the initial investment, since Ethiopian household benefit-cost ratios were 0.42 to 0.78 at market wages and exceeded one only with a shadow wage and a low initial investment [ev_economic_return_schmidt12_6]; where structures are built, since off-farm community works gave no food-security or income effect [ev_food_security_abate21_4, ev_food_security_arega24_1, ev_household_income_abate21_2]; the rainfall year [ev_food_security_kabo04_1]; and how long benefits are counted, since the Brazilian ratio covers a short window against a long-lived asset and counts income only [ev_economic_return_casag22_9]. For a Task Team Leader, the practical points are targeting smallholders, costing household labour honestly and expecting returns to arrive over years. On quality, the largest gains are from bundled programmes with weak attribution, and the Brazilian income effects are for a cistern bundled with a productive grant and training, not the cistern alone [ev_household_income_casag22_1]: IEG calls the China income estimate not robust and notes the India gains may partly be construction wages, and a Karnataka completion report doubts its own before/after figures [ev_household_income_iegchn07_6, ev_household_income_iegind11_2, ev_household_income_kar20_3]. The losses and nulls come mostly from independent evaluations, though the Ethiopian negative values may omit off-site benefits [ev_economic_return_adim16_4], and a Kenyan bundle showed no effect on per capita income [ev_household_income_mala24_2]. Income, returns and food security are proxies for poverty, and the Malawi food-security finding is qualitative and cited second-hand [ev_food_security_ngur26_1]. A cited Burkina Faso statement adds that higher yields improve household food security especially on farms applying manure or some kind of soil and water conservation on over half their plots; it sits on the gain side but does not separate manure from conservation [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5].

effect_mechanism: Zai pits, planting pits, contour bunds and reduced or ripper tillage raise and stabilise yields in dry years: compilers describe planting pits in Uganda keeping banana stands fruiting through drought and raising monthly harvests for sale, composting with planting pits in Burkina Faso raising farm income several times in dry years, and the Magoye ripper in Zambia improving yields and tolerance to dry spells at lower tillage cost [ev_food_security_wocat_1587_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1587_2013_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_959_2010_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1139_2013_farm_income]. In the literature, returns to labour for these practices in Burkina Faso exceed the shadow wage, and bunds show positive returns at subproject level in Mauritania [ev_economic_return_kabo04_1, ev_economic_return_mrt14_5]. Compilers also judge benefits to outweigh establishment and maintenance costs in both the short and the long term on every sheet that rates them. In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers earned a maize gross margin of 473.36 USD per hectare against 70.60 on conventional plots in the low-rainfall budget, with 866.84 against 357.16 for experienced farmers in high rainfall [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2], and ground cover raised the odds of a Malawian plot meeting the household maize requirement in the El Niño season, and planting basins sharply raised those odds in a good Kenyan season [ev_food_security_boil19_1, ev_food_security_boil19_2]. Against the fertilised conventional arm in the same Zimbabwe budget the first-year margin was 473.36 against 48.19 US dollars per hectare [ev_economic_return_mazv09_3]. In Zimbabwe's El Niño season, no-till with a residue mulch returned a cost-benefit ratio of 1.39 against 1.05 for conventional tillage [ev_economic_return_mash25h1_3]. A review cites reduced tillage with residue maintained giving the highest net benefit and marginal rate of return on teff [ev_economic_return_tade23h1_4]. conditionality: This row now holds conflicting evidence. What pulls the in-field side apart is how the gain is valued and against what. justification.mechanism: Zai pits, planting pits, contour bunds and reduced or ripper tillage raise and stabilise yields in dry years: compilers describe planting pits in Uganda keeping banana stands fruiting through drought and raising monthly harvests for sale, composting with planting pits in Burkina Faso raising farm income several times in dry years, and the Magoye ripper in Zambia improving yields and tolerance to dry spells at lower tillage cost [ev_food_security_wocat_1587_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1587_2013_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_959_2010_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1139_2013_farm_income]. In the literature, returns to labour for these practices in Burkina Faso exceed the shadow wage, and bunds show positive returns at subproject level in Mauritania [ev_economic_return_kabo04_1, ev_economic_return_mrt14_5]. Compilers also judge benefits to outweigh establishment and maintenance costs in both the short and the long term on every sheet that rates them. In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers earned a maize gross margin of 473.36 USD per hectare against 70.60 on conventional plots in the low-rainfall budget, with 866.84 against 357.16 for experienced farmers in high rainfall [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2], and ground cover raised the odds of a Malawian plot meeting the household maize requirement in the El Niño season, and planting basins sharply raised those odds in a good Kenyan season [ev_food_security_boil19_1, ev_food_security_boil19_2]. Against the fertilised conventional arm in the same Zimbabwe budget the first-year margin was 473.36 against 48.19 US dollars per hectare [ev_economic_return_mazv09_3]. In Zimbabwe's El Niño season, no-till with a residue mulch returned a cost-benefit ratio of 1.39 against 1.05 for conventional tillage [ev_economic_return_mash25h1_3]. A review cites reduced tillage with residue maintained giving the highest net benefit and marginal rate of return on teff [ev_economic_return_tade23h1_4]. In Zambia, crop budgets for hand-hoe conservation-farming basins give returns per hectare 70 percent higher than conventional hand hoe cultivation and 150 percent higher than conventional plowing for cotton, and returns to land and to peak-season labor 60 to 90 percent higher than hand hoe tillage for maize [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_hagg03_7, ev_economic_return_hagg03_8].
justification.conditionality: This row now holds conflicting evidence. What pulls the in-field side apart is how the gain is valued and against what. Crop budgets built on bundled input packages, and the practitioner ratings, put basins well ahead [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_hagg03_8, ev_economic_return_mazv09_1]; but a Zimbabwe household panel that values predicted yields with inputs held constant finds conservation agriculture (mostly planting basins, with residue mulch and rotation on some plots) generates less revenue than traditional cultivation over a large portion of the rainfall distribution, and its revenue comes out ahead only when rainfall is far from the mean [ev_economic_return_mich19_8]. The other losses are season- or practice-specific: banking in Malawi's El Nino season, tied ridging in a Kenyan drought season, and 30-cm zaï on a Burkina Faso trial [ev_food_security_boil19_3, ev_economic_return_ndun23_1, ev_economic_return_zour25h1_4]. Most units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets, including the benefit-versus-cost judgements; the literature units are secondary model estimates for Burkina Faso and a lender self-reported subproject evaluation for Mauritania, and manual zai gives far smaller net benefits than mechanised zai in the same source [ev_economic_return_kabo04_1, ev_economic_return_mrt14_5, ev_economic_return_zoug14_1]. Several rated technologies bundle pits with compost or are conservation-tillage systems, and food security and farm income are proxies for poverty [ev_household_income_wocat_959_2010_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1139_2013_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Cost savings from conservation agriculture are usually small for smallholders, and in a Kenyan drought season net benefits were higher without tied ridging except with Tithonia [ev_economic_return_corb20_1, ev_economic_return_ndun23_1]; the Zimbabwe margins include manure and fertiliser with the high-rainfall figure a sensitivity scenario, and the Kenyan planting-basin odds ratio has a wide confidence interval [ev_economic_return_mazv09_2, ev_food_security_boil19_2]. In Malawi's El Nino season banking lowered the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement from 0.19 to 0.054, so a mis-timed in-field practice can cut food security rather than raise it [ev_food_security_boil19_3]. 30-cm zaï on the same Burkina Faso trial ran at a loss (−98 624 FCFA per hectare), smaller than the direct-seeding loss, and the investment counted is the experiment's own cost [ev_economic_return_zour25h1_4]. The Zimbabwe ratio is a single drought-season budget with the mulch bundled with no-till [ev_economic_return_mash25h1_3]. The teff returns are cited second-hand [ev_economic_return_tade23h1_4]. The Zambian returns are crop budgets with output estimated from regression coefficients, bundled with early planting and purchased inputs (hybrid seed and fertiliser for maize), and the authors say early-planting gains dominate the maize results [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_hagg03_8]. The Zimbabwe panel figure is gross revenue at later market prices with labour and non-market inputs unvalued, so it is neither a profit nor a poverty measure [ev_economic_return_mich19_8].

effect_mechanism: Small reservoirs, sand dams, farm ponds, runoff cisterns and subsurface dams provide water for dry-season irrigation of vegetables and fruit and for livestock, shifting cropping towards higher-value crops and raising household income and lean-season food security [ev_household_income_veno12_2, ev_household_income_ritc21_3, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6]. WOCAT compilers add that farm ponds in Cambodia keep enough irrigation water through drought, gully check dams in Ethiopia free rangeland for grazing, and gully rehabilitation in Somalia raised crop and livestock productivity [ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6716_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_7778_2026_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Compilers' benefit-versus-cost ratings are positive or very positive over the long term for every sheet that rates them. In Kenya, farmers living near sand dams saw average income rise by 60% as more water in dry periods raised farm yields [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. Reviews add that rainwater-harvesting ponds brought statistically significant gains in household income and food security in Burkina Faso, water storage gave Ethiopian smallholders greater income security, harvested water used with precision irrigation in Ethiopia reached a net water value of up to 1.53 USD per cubic metre, and benefit-cost ratios of up to 3.38 with payback periods of 6.8 to 12 years; Indian farms with a farm pond reported net returns of 857 USD per hectare against 586 without [ev_household_income_silv26_1, ev_household_income_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_silv26_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. In Brazil, an Embrapa survey of some communities found small-farm incomes rose by about half a minimum wage per month after the second filling of the barraginhas, and adopters rated food security as the technology's largest impact [ev_household_income_mira19_1, ev_food_security_mira19_2].
conditionality: Most literature magnitudes are secondary citations in reviews or vote counts, and practitioner ratings make up a large share of the pool [ev_household_income_saru19_3, ev_household_income_veno12_3]. Sand dams are judged likely not cost-efficient for water supply, Brazilian subsurface dams produced little cash income where electricity, investment capital or an irrigation tradition were missing, and the high Brazilian benefit-cost ratios come from an upper-middle-income context [ev_economic_return_ritc21_1, ev_household_income_cirilo03_7, ev_economic_return_cirilo03_10]. Compilers rate check-dam land in China as raising the risk of production failure in extreme wet years and an Indian subsistence farm pond as leaving farm income unchanged; Kenyan sand dams are embedded in a wider food-security programme [ev_food_security_wocat_1455_2011_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1474_2011_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1537_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Short-term returns on establishment are rated slightly to very negative on sheets from Tunisia, China, Nicaragua and Somalia, and the cost-benefit units are compiler judgements, not measured returns. The Kenyan sand-dam income rise compares a small sample of households with a control catchment [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. The reviewed income, water-value and benefit-cost figures are secondary citations, reported at their upper end, and the Indian pond returns come from a cross-sectional preprint survey confounded by farm size and assets [ev_economic_return_silv26_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. The barraginha income and food-security findings are Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, from an informal survey and adopter ratings with no normal-year reference [ev_household_income_mira19_1, ev_food_security_mira19_2].

A review reports terraces reducing net crop income in Ethiopia and banquette profitability in Niger was close to nil; compilers record no change in food security for vetiver terraces in Haiti, where farmers must wait for degraded soil to recover, and on sheets from Rwanda [ev_household_income_mala24_1, ev_economic_return_heusch95_1, ev_food_security_wocat_3223_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. effect_mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and lines, banquettes, trenches, pits and check dams slow overland flow and spread it behind barriers, so less runoff leaves the slope and less soil is detached and carried away; check dams and gabions trap sediment in channels. Measured reductions are large: terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, Burundi terrace plots cut erosion by 50% to 90%, trenches reduced soil loss by 73.0% on average, and check dams cut catchment sediment export by 20 to 98% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_1, ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1]. WOCAT compilers across many countries rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as reduced, explaining that micro-catchments cut the kinetic energy of rain by trapping runoff and that check dams slow runoff so soil accumulates upstream [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_2895_2017_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_soil_loss]. Meta-analyses confirm the direction: a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds soil loss cut by 58.66% and runoff by 53% on average, with soil-loss reductions of 68.67% for mulching, 54.97% for ridging, 55.06% for soil and stone bunds and 60.21% for terraces [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_1, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_1, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_2, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_3, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_4, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_5]; an Ethiopian synthesis reports soil loss down 59% under graded soil bunds, 88% under level soil bunds, 38% under stone bunds, 98% under mulch and 62% under tied ridging [ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_1, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_2, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_3, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_4, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_5]; and a terracing meta-analysis finds erosion control on terraces 11.46 times that of controls and runoff reduction 2.6 times [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_1]. At catchment scale, stone bunds, check dams and regrowth in Ethiopia cut sediment yield from 8.5 to 1.9 t per hectare a year, and check dams on China's Loess Plateau reduced erosion rates from more than 200 to 20–25 t per hectare a year [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_luca21_1]. A meta-analysis of mulching finds runoff reduced by 47.4% and soil loss by 76.2% against controls, soil loss by 70.9% on cropland, and reductions of 45.9% and 75.1% at rainfall intensities above 90 mm/h [ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_1, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_2, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_3, ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_5, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_6]. In Brazil, barraginhas dispersed across farms capture runoff water, which Embrapa says prevents erosion, siltation and the carrying of pollutants [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5].
conditionality: Over two thirds of the pool are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets, and several literature sources are lender self-reports with before/after designs, perception surveys or catchment numbers that barely changed: the Rwanda sediment drop from 54 to 2.6 tons/ha a year has no control, and Indian sediment yield moved only from 71.6 to 69.3 tons per ha per year [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_utk22_3, ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5]; runoff reduction and sediment retention enter as component proxies. Negative findings: check dams can cause downstream channel incision, diversion banquettes increased gully and bank erosion in Niger, trenches raised sediment in the first years, Maghreb banquettes were often erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. Some sheets rate no change, including the Indian farm-pond sheet, and the Zambian tillage sheet expects less downstream siltation only if applied on a large scale [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_siltation]. A catchment-restoration meta-analysis in Ethiopia finds minimal effect of catchment treatment on runoff in drought-prone areas with annual rainfall below 500 mm [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_3]. In Tunisia gullied area on banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, poorly maintained banquettes in Algeria accelerate erosion, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]; and USA check dams had no significant effect on the runoff volume of major storms [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2]. The meta-analyses pool unweighted study means and are dominated by plot-scale East African studies, so catchment-scale effects remain less certain [ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1]. The mulching meta-analysis pools land uses including post-fire forest and bare land; cropland and tree crops were less effective in reducing runoff, both below 40%, and the mulching benefits decreased with increasing rainfall intensity under heavy rainfall [ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_4, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_6]. The barraginha erosion statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measurement [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5].

family_vote.rule: family rows vote with weight sqrt(n_sources); dissent >= 0.33 of signed weight -> conflicting_evidence (Pete 2026-10-19, rollup_family_honesty B)

justification.mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and lines, banquettes, trenches, pits and check dams slow overland flow and spread it behind barriers, so less runoff leaves the slope and less soil is detached and carried away; check dams and gabions trap sediment in channels. Measured reductions are large: terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, Burundi terrace plots cut erosion by 50% to 90%, trenches reduced soil loss by 73.0% on average, and check dams cut catchment sediment export by 20 to 98% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_1, ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1]. WOCAT compilers across many countries rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as reduced, explaining that micro-catchments cut the kinetic energy of rain by trapping runoff and that check dams slow runoff so soil accumulates upstream [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_2895_2017_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_soil_loss]. Meta-analyses confirm the direction: a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds soil loss cut by 58.66% and runoff by 53% on average, with soil-loss reductions of 68.67% for mulching, 54.97% for ridging, 55.06% for soil and stone bunds and 60.21% for terraces [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_1, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_1, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_2, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_3, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_4, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_5]; an Ethiopian synthesis reports soil loss down 59% under graded soil bunds, 88% under level soil bunds, 38% under stone bunds, 98% under mulch and 62% under tied ridging [ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_1, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_2, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_3, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_4, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_5]; and a terracing meta-analysis finds erosion control on terraces 11.46 times that of controls and runoff reduction 2.6 times [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_1]. At catchment scale, stone bunds, check dams and regrowth in Ethiopia cut sediment yield from 8.5 to 1.9 t per hectare a year, and check dams on China's Loess Plateau reduced erosion rates from more than 200 to 20–25 t per hectare a year [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_luca21_1]. A meta-analysis of mulching finds runoff reduced by 47.4% and soil loss by 76.2% against controls, soil loss by 70.9% on cropland, and reductions of 45.9% and 75.1% at rainfall intensities above 90 mm/h [ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_1, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_2, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_3, ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_5, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_6]. In Brazil, barraginhas dispersed across farms capture runoff water, which Embrapa says prevents erosion, siltation and the carrying of pollutants [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5].
justification.conditionality: Over two thirds of the pool are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets, and several literature sources are lender self-reports with before/after designs, perception surveys or catchment numbers that barely changed: the Rwanda sediment drop from 54 to 2.6 tons/ha a year has no control, and Indian sediment yield moved only from 71.6 to 69.3 tons per ha per year [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_utk22_3, ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5]; runoff reduction and sediment retention enter as component proxies. Negative findings: check dams can cause downstream channel incision, diversion banquettes increased gully and bank erosion in Niger, trenches raised sediment in the first years, Maghreb banquettes were often erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. Some sheets rate no change, including the Indian farm-pond sheet, and the Zambian tillage sheet expects less downstream siltation only if applied on a large scale [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_siltation]. A catchment-restoration meta-analysis in Ethiopia finds minimal effect of catchment treatment on runoff in drought-prone areas with annual rainfall below 500 mm [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_3]. In Tunisia gullied area on banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, poorly maintained banquettes in Algeria accelerate erosion, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]; and USA check dams had no significant effect on the runoff volume of major storms [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2]. The meta-analyses pool unweighted study means and are dominated by plot-scale East African studies, so catchment-scale effects remain less certain [ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1]. The mulching meta-analysis pools land uses including post-fire forest and bare land; cropland and tree crops were less effective in reducing runoff, both below 40%, and the mulching benefits decreased with increasing rainfall intensity under heavy rainfall [ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_4, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_6]. The barraginha erosion statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measurement [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5].

effect_mechanism: In the Maghreb, contour structures have been reported both to hold runoff and to accelerate erosion. Staggered earth bunds (tabia) in Morocco store the runoff of all rains below 50 mm on the field [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. In Algeria, a poorly maintained banquette becomes a factor accelerating erosion, because the smallest unrepaired breach triggers a chain reaction through the whole network in torrential and prolonged rains [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].
conditionality: Two conditions separate the sides in the sources. Maintenance: the acceleration is tied explicitly to unrepaired breaches in state-built banquettes [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2]. Storm size: the tabia hold runoff only up to rains of 50 mm, and in bigger storms the excess overtops them and gullies the whole slope [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. The actionable reading is to plan and fund upkeep and spillways, not only construction. Elsewhere banquettes simply did not stop gullying: gullied areas on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, and over 1947-1968 Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. Neither side is measured on plots: the protective statement is from an expert manual and the harmful ones are secondary citations within a national evaluation, and the two concern different structures, tabia and banquettes [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].

effect_mechanism: Physical SWC works under public-works and watershed programmes reduce soil loss and downstream runoff, and sediment-control dams with terraces and vegetation trap sediment in the catchment. A meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds soil loss cut by 58.66% and runoff by 53% on average, with soil and stone bunds reducing soil loss by 55.06% and runoff by 49.2% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_1, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_1, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_4, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_5]; in Ethiopian catchments, stone bunds, check dams and vegetation regrowth cut sediment yield from 8.5 to 1.9 t per hectare a year [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_2].
conditionality: Nearly all units are programme or lender reports from Ethiopia, India and China, often perception surveys or before/after comparisons; an Uttarakhand water budget showed surface runoff slightly increasing, the Karnataka runoff comparison is against another SWC programme, and IEG doubts the India runoff measurements. Effects mixing runoff and soil-loss metrics are only components of erosion risk. A catchment-restoration meta-analysis in Ethiopia finds minimal effect of catchment treatment on runoff in drought-prone areas with annual rainfall below 500 mm [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_3]. effect_mechanism: Infiltration trenches intercept and infiltrate runoff, cutting plot-level runoff and soil loss, with the runoff reduction larger on natural vegetation than on cropland [ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_1, ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_2]. WOCAT compilers rate zai and planting pits, contour bunds, basin tillage and conservation tillage as reducing soil loss and surface runoff, the Zambian ripper sheet attributing this to less soil disturbance and better soil cover [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1139_2013_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1139_2013_surface_runoff]. Meta-analyses now quantify the effect: a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds soil loss cut by 68.67% under mulching and 54.97% under ridging and runoff by 57.2% and 53.6% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_2, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_3, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_2, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_4]; an Ethiopian synthesis reports soil loss down 59% under graded soil bunds, 88% under level soil bunds, 98% under mulch and 62% under tied ridging, with runoff down 25.2%, 60.1%, 75.5% and 55.8% [ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_1, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_2, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_4, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_5, ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_1, ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_2, ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_5, ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_4]; tied ridging in India reduced runoff by 69%, reviews report zai and tassa pits cutting runoff by 60–80% and high mulch cover by up to 79%, and Moroccan tabia store the runoff of all rains below 50 mm [ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_7, ev_runoff_reduction_ngur26_1, ev_runoff_reduction_ngur26_2, ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. A meta-analysis of mulching finds runoff reduced by 47.4% and soil loss by 76.2% against controls, soil loss by 70.9% on cropland, and reductions of 45.9% and 75.1% at rainfall intensities above 90 mm/h [ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_1, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_2, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_3, ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_5, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_6].
conditionality: The literature units all come from a single review of trenches, largely in the Peruvian Andes (upper-middle income), which also reports increased catchment sediment in the first years after construction; plot-level effects may not transfer to catchments [ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_3]. The rest are practitioner ratings, several for conservation-tillage systems, and the Zambian sheet expects reduced downstream siltation only if applied on a large scale [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_siltation]. Tabia overflow and gully the slope in the biggest storms [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]; the meta-analytic figures are unweighted means of plot studies and the pit and mulch ranges are review syntheses [ev_runoff_reduction_ngur26_1]. The mulching meta-analysis pools land uses including post-fire forest and bare land; cropland and tree crops were less effective in reducing runoff, both below 40%, and the mulching benefits decreased with increasing rainfall intensity under heavy rainfall [ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_4, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_6].

justification.conditionality: The literature units all come from a single review of trenches, largely in the Peruvian Andes (upper-middle income), which also reports increased catchment sediment in the first years after construction; plot-level effects may not transfer to catchments [ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_3]. The rest are practitioner ratings, several for conservation-tillage systems, and the Zambian sheet expects reduced downstream siltation only if applied on a large scale [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_siltation]. effect_mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, contour stone bunds and lines and banquettes shorten slope length and slow runoff, so soil losses on steep plots fall sharply and sediment loads drop where terracing is widespread. Terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots on 20 to 60% slopes from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, a contour banquette in Niger divided erosion by 150 against traditional cropping, and stone bunds with compost cut total soil loss by 79% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_1]. WOCAT compilers rate soil loss and runoff as reduced on terraces from China to Uzbekistan, noting that stone lines in Tunisia cut runoff by 50% and that Gradoni terraces trap soil eroded from the inter-spaces [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_6610_2022_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1522_2010_surface_runoff]. Meta-analyses agree: a terracing meta-analysis finds erosion control on terraces 11.46 times that of controls and runoff reduction 2.6 times [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_1], a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds terraces cut soil loss by 60.21% and runoff by 56.5%, and an Ethiopian synthesis reports stone bunds cutting soil loss by 38% and runoff by 34.4% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_5, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_3, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_3, ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_3]. Reviews also report terracing reducing runoff by 92.6% and 80% in sub-humid and humid regions, stone lines and terraces reducing runoff and erosion by 30 to 50%, sediment accumulating behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, and fanya juu trapping 64% of sediment, rising to 80% with vetiver grass [ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_2, ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_3, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6].
conditionality: Alignment decides the sign: diversion banquettes in Niger doubled runoff coefficients and increased gully erosion, while contour banquettes in the same region cut erosion; ditches with downslope banks cause rill erosion, many Maghreb banquettes were erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. The Rwanda sediment reductions are lender-monitored before/after figures without a control, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements rather than measurements [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_2]. Bench terracing alone reduced runoff by only 9% in a small USA watershed, gullied area on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, poorly maintained Algerian banquettes accelerate erosion, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on downstream dam sedimentation [ev_runoff_reduction_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. The meta-analytic ratios are unweighted, and the Ethiopian stone-bund sediment figure comes with a total soil loss of 77 t per hectare, so bunds trap most but not all eroded soil [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1].

justification.pool_note: This row draws on 73 evidence unit(s) from 29 source(s); the weighting counts sources, not units, so several findings from one paper do not multiply its say.
justification.mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, contour stone bunds and lines and banquettes shorten slope length and slow runoff, so soil losses on steep plots fall sharply and sediment loads drop where terracing is widespread. Terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots on 20 to 60% slopes from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, a contour banquette in Niger divided erosion by 150 against traditional cropping, and stone bunds with compost cut total soil loss by 79% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_1]. WOCAT compilers rate soil loss and runoff as reduced on terraces from China to Uzbekistan, noting that stone lines in Tunisia cut runoff by 50% and that Gradoni terraces trap soil eroded from the inter-spaces [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_6610_2022_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1522_2010_surface_runoff]. Meta-analyses agree: a terracing meta-analysis finds erosion control on terraces 11.46 times that of controls and runoff reduction 2.6 times [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_1], a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds terraces cut soil loss by 60.21% and runoff by 56.5%, and an Ethiopian synthesis reports stone bunds cutting soil loss by 38% and runoff by 34.4% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_5, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_3, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_3, ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_3]. Reviews also report terracing reducing runoff by 92.6% and 80% in sub-humid and humid regions, stone lines and terraces reducing runoff and erosion by 30 to 50%, sediment accumulating behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, and fanya juu trapping 64% of sediment, rising to 80% with vetiver grass [ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_2, ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_3, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6].
justification.conditionality: Alignment decides the sign: diversion banquettes in Niger doubled runoff coefficients and increased gully erosion, while contour banquettes in the same region cut erosion; ditches with downslope banks cause rill erosion, many Maghreb banquettes were erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. The Rwanda sediment reductions are lender-monitored before/after figures without a control, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements rather than measurements [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_2]. Bench terracing alone reduced runoff by only 9% in a small USA watershed, gullied area on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, poorly maintained Algerian banquettes accelerate erosion, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on downstream dam sedimentation [ev_runoff_reduction_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. The meta-analytic ratios are unweighted, and the Ethiopian stone-bund sediment figure comes with a total soil loss of 77 t per hectare, so bunds trap most but not all eroded soil [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1].

effect_mechanism: Check dams, gabions, fascines, terraces and bunds trap sediment that would otherwise reach streams, canals and reservoirs, lowering catchment sediment export and downstream siltation [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. WOCAT compilers describe gabion walls and check dams in Somalia trapping sediment upstream and reducing siltation of downstream fields and water bodies, and vegetative check dams in Madagascar reducing siltation of downstream rice fields [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6478_2022_downstream_siltation]. Measured retention now spans scales: check dams on China's Loess Plateau are credited with cutting regional sediment export by about 85% and accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction at the outlets of five catchments over 26 years, and loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of watershed sediment yield [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1]; sediment accumulates behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, fanya juu trapped 64% of sediment (80% with vetiver grass), and bench terracing cut sediment yield by 58% in a small USA watershed [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5]; and small ponds trapped 54-85% of incoming sediment over 8 years in southern Germany and 68% over the long term in Belgium [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. Holding soil also holds nutrients: an Ethiopian synthesis finds graded soil bunds reduced total nitrogen lost in runoff and sediment by up to 48% [ev_nutrient_removal_adim16_1].
conditionality: The class follows the sub-practice vote, not the pooled result. The in-field row holds the strongest result, strong positive, but it rests on WOCAT ratings for pits, stone lines and contour bunds in Niger and conservation tillage in Kenya and Zambia, plus the Ethiopian graded-bund nitrogen synthesis [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1100_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1219_2014_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1652_2014_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_940_2010_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_siltation, ev_nutrient_removal_adim16_1]. The rows that carry the measured trapping studies — check dams and ponds (runoff catchment) and terraces and bunds (terracing) — hold moderate positive, as do the micro-catchment and spate rows; the cross-family row, a single modelled Chinese programme figure, holds slight positive [ev_sediment_retention_iegchn07_5]. The weighted median is moderate positive, below the pooled strong. Water quality is inferred almost entirely from sediment retention, a component proxy, plus nutrient losses in runoff from a single synthesis; nothing on water chemistry downstream is measured, and many units are practitioner ratings of downstream siltation from WOCAT sheets. Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of a downstream dam over 1947-1968, and the twofold decline in outlet sediment yield with USA check dams was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Much of the literature is secondary citations in reviews, several from high-income settings (USA, Germany, Belgium), the China programme figure is modelled, and gabions in Morocco have filled and need raising [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_iegchn07_5, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1]. A sheet from Niger rates siltation unchanged, the Zambian tillage sheet expects a benefit only at large scale, and the Ethiopian compiler notes the trapped sediment has not been quantified [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1614_2014_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_siltation].

justification.mechanism: Terracing and retaining walls hold soil on slopes, which an evaluation in Morocco expects to reduce siltation of downstream rivers and dam storage [ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. WOCAT compilers rate downstream siltation as reduced for radical terraces in Rwanda, bench terraces in Yemen and Bangladesh, stone lines in Uganda and Tunisia, contour stone bunds in Niger and vetiver terraces in Haiti [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1553_2012_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1560_2013_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1616_2014_downstream_siltation]. Reviews add that sediment accumulates behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, fanya juu trapped 64% of sediment (80% with vetiver grass), and bench terracing cut sediment yield by 58% in a small USA watershed [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5].
justification.conditionality: The Morocco unit is an evaluator assertion and the rest are practitioner ratings; nothing on water chemistry is measured, and siltation is a component proxy [ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. The Gradoni terrace sheet for Uzbekistan rates only a slight reduction [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_7553_2025_downstream_siltation]. The added sediment figures are secondary citations in a review, the bench-terrace figure comes from a high-income watershed, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of a downstream dam over 1947-1968 [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1].

effect_mechanism: Bunds, stone lines, micro-basins and check dams capture and retain rainwater so that it infiltrates, and compilers and local people report raised well levels; sand dams and subsurface dams store water that extends the months of water access or backs up wells when other sources dry up, production cisterns keep livestock watered, and participating villages in India reduced water transport by tanker. WOCAT compilers for jessour, spate and water-spreading systems, bunds, terraces, check dams, sand dams, ponds and haffirs from Tunisia, Niger, Ethiopia, Kenya, India, Somalia and elsewhere judge them to improve water harvesting, water quantity or water availability. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1]. A check-dam review reports that check dams storing seasonal runoff solve local supply scarcity; traditional rainwater ponds in South Korea reduced the occurrence of water deficit from 30 to 20% [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. In India, discharge of springs and streams rose in treated watersheds: a sample study in Himachal Pradesh reports a 40 percent increase in water discharge in spring and stream sources [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1], and the Uttarakhand project achieved an average 21 percent increase in water discharge from perennial water sources in sampled micro-watersheds, against a target of 25 percent [ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Measured soil moisture adds a field-level route: capture structures hold rain in the root zone. A meta-analysis of in-situ practices finds they improve soil moisture retention by 59%, with infiltration pits highest at an SMD of 114.4%, soil/stone bunds 76.4%, tied ridging 48.9% and terraces 40.5% [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_2, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_3, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_5, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_6]; a global terracing synthesis finds terraced sites more efficient than slopes at conserving soil water, with a mean δsm of 1.2 [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1]; and conversion of slopeland to leveled fields in China increased moisture retention [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells, and zaï can retain moisture in the soil for seven to ten days after rainfall [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8]. In Brazil tied furrows kept more soil moisture than the traditional flat system at all crop stages and depths [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9], and in Ethiopia hand-dug planting basins held more topsoil water than unmulched plots at Ziway at flowering and maturity [ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_4, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_6]. Mulching, the soil-cover form of in-situ water harvesting, improves soil moisture retention with an SMD of 54.0% in the meta-analysis, and maize-stalk mulch in Ethiopia held more topsoil water than unmulched plots at Ziway at all three stages [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_4, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_1, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_3, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_5]. Indian project watersheds showed an increase in soil moisture content by 30.5 percent compared to the IWMP sites [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. Grain per unit of rain rises with capture in a set of East and Southern African trials: the best conservation-farming practice per site gave yield increases ranging from 20 to 120% over conventional tillage whilst rain water productivity improved with 10–50% [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. In an on-farm trial at Houndé, Burkina Faso, stone rows with zaï pits, every arm also receiving manure, lifted maize rain water productivity from 3.10 kg per hectare per mm under the farmers' practice of oxen ploughing with NPK and urea to 6.61 [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_1]. A review reports that contour tied-ridging in eastern Sudan gave the highest water use efficiency of the treatments compared [ev_rain_water_productivity_ngur26_3]. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. The FAO compilers rate improving water productivity at the top of their scale for the conservation agriculture group [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_2]. They rate improving water productivity for the cross-slope barrier group at the middle mark of their scale [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. For the WOCAT water harvesting groups the guideline authors' marks for improving water productivity run from the lowest positive mark for floodwater and microcatchment harvesting to the middle mark for macrocatchment harvesting [ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_4, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_3].
conditionality: Most literature units are narrative, perception or lender-reported, the pooled percentages mix spring-discharge, water-deficit and tanker-use metrics, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets rather than measurements; compilers judge no change in water availability for water spreading in Sudan and semi-circular bunds in Niger, and Ethiopian compilers note that off-site effects of recently built structures are yet to be assessed [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1614_2014_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6715_2023_water_availability]. Groundwater-recharge evidence, with its limits, now sits in the catchment water yield rows. Many sand dams cannot supply a household through the dry season [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3]. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2]. The check-dam and pond findings are secondary citations in reviews, and the Korean result is modelled in a high-income setting [ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. The Indian spring and stream discharge figures come from World Bank completion reports, the lender's own evaluation, measured before and after without untreated comparison sites, for catchment treatment that bundles plantations, trenches, ponds and check dams with water-harvesting structures, so the gain cannot be credited to water harvesting alone [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1, ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. What upstream capture does to water downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows. The measured soil-moisture evidence has its own limits. Tillage alone is not water harvesting: in the Brazilian trial deep ploughing, which is tillage alone, scored as high as the tied furrows, so that treatment does not speak for the practice [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. The Ethiopian basins did not differ from unmulched plots at planting at Ziway or at any stage at Melkassa [ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_2, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_8, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_10, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_12]. Under meteorological drought and dry spells in Kenya, tied ridging without organic inputs was insufficient in soil moisture conservation since there was little or no rainwater to be held in the basins [ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]: structures store rain, they cannot make it. A review found no significant effect of infiltration trenches on soil moisture because only four studies provided sufficient statistical data [ev_soil_water_retention_locat20_1]. The zaï and half-moon results come with compost in the pits, so the moisture gain cannot be credited to the pit alone [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8], the Indian watershed comparison is a project-commissioned study of a package of soil and water conservation structures [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2], and the Brazilian tied-furrow trial ran a single season at a station of the agency that promotes the technology [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. Soil moisture is read as a component of water stress, not water stress itself. Those best-practice arms are bundled: planting pits, basins or ripper-with-ridging (the capture element, which is the practice here) come with reduced tillage and mostly with fertiliser, and tillage alone is not water harvesting [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. The trial-level readings are weaker: the authors find no clear tillage effect on rain water productivity in Kenya, no clear effects of tillage in Ethiopia (where the gains that do show come with fertilised treatments), and only a tendency of improvement in semi-arid Tanzania [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_5, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_4]. The Burkina Faso trial covers a single season, and every conservation arm also received manure, so its gain belongs to the package rather than to the structures alone [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_1]. At Houndé, grass strips with zaï (4.84 against 3.10) were not significantly different from the control, and at Péni neither grass strips with zaï (4.51) nor earth bunds with contour ploughing (4.31) differed significantly from the control (3.53), the authors stating that water was not limiting at Péni, which had more rain than Houndé that season [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_4]. The Sudan comparison ranks treatments without a no-practice value [ev_rain_water_productivity_ngur26_3]. These are compiler and author judgements across groups, direction only, and the review sentence is second-hand; the WOCAT authors also note that some case studies indicate little to no improvement in water use efficiency [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. The FAO and WOCAT group marks are compiler judgements, direction only, and the conservation agriculture group bundles mulch with minimum tillage and rotation [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_4].

justification.mechanism: Bunds, stone lines, micro-basins and check dams capture and retain rainwater so that it infiltrates, and compilers and local people report raised well levels; sand dams and subsurface dams store water that extends the months of water access or backs up wells when other sources dry up, production cisterns keep livestock watered, and participating villages in India reduced water transport by tanker. WOCAT compilers for jessour, spate and water-spreading systems, bunds, terraces, check dams, sand dams, ponds and haffirs from Tunisia, Niger, Ethiopia, Kenya, India, Somalia and elsewhere judge them to improve water harvesting, water quantity or water availability. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1]. A check-dam review reports that check dams storing seasonal runoff solve local supply scarcity; traditional rainwater ponds in South Korea reduced the occurrence of water deficit from 30 to 20% [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. In India, discharge of springs and streams rose in treated watersheds: a sample study in Himachal Pradesh reports a 40 percent increase in water discharge in spring and stream sources [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1], and the Uttarakhand project achieved an average 21 percent increase in water discharge from perennial water sources in sampled micro-watersheds, against a target of 25 percent [ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Measured soil moisture adds a field-level route: capture structures hold rain in the root zone. A meta-analysis of in-situ practices finds they improve soil moisture retention by 59%, with infiltration pits highest at an SMD of 114.4%, soil/stone bunds 76.4%, tied ridging 48.9% and terraces 40.5% [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_2, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_3, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_5, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_6]; a global terracing synthesis finds terraced sites more efficient than slopes at conserving soil water, with a mean δsm of 1.2 [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1]; and conversion of slopeland to leveled fields in China increased moisture retention [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells, and zaï can retain moisture in the soil for seven to ten days after rainfall [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8]. In Brazil tied furrows kept more soil moisture than the traditional flat system at all crop stages and depths [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9], and in Ethiopia hand-dug planting basins held more topsoil water than unmulched plots at Ziway at flowering and maturity [ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_4, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_6]. Mulching, the soil-cover form of in-situ water harvesting, improves soil moisture retention with an SMD of 54.0% in the meta-analysis, and maize-stalk mulch in Ethiopia held more topsoil water than unmulched plots at Ziway at all three stages [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_4, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_1, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_3, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_5]. Indian project watersheds showed an increase in soil moisture content by 30.5 percent compared to the IWMP sites [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. Grain per unit of rain rises with capture in a set of East and Southern African trials: the best conservation-farming practice per site gave yield increases ranging from 20 to 120% over conventional tillage whilst rain water productivity improved with 10–50% [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. In an on-farm trial at Houndé, Burkina Faso, stone rows with zaï pits, every arm also receiving manure, lifted maize rain water productivity from 3.10 kg per hectare per mm under the farmers' practice of oxen ploughing with NPK and urea to 6.61 [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_1]. A review reports that contour tied-ridging in eastern Sudan gave the highest water use efficiency of the treatments compared [ev_rain_water_productivity_ngur26_3]. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. The FAO compilers rate improving water productivity at the top of their scale for the conservation agriculture group [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_2]. They rate improving water productivity for the cross-slope barrier group at the middle mark of their scale [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. For the WOCAT water harvesting groups the guideline authors' marks for improving water productivity run from the lowest positive mark for floodwater and microcatchment harvesting to the middle mark for macrocatchment harvesting [ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_4, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_3].
justification.conditionality: Most literature units are narrative, perception or lender-reported, the pooled percentages mix spring-discharge, water-deficit and tanker-use metrics, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets rather than measurements; compilers judge no change in water availability for water spreading in Sudan and semi-circular bunds in Niger, and Ethiopian compilers note that off-site effects of recently built structures are yet to be assessed [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1614_2014_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6715_2023_water_availability]. Groundwater-recharge evidence, with its limits, now sits in the catchment water yield rows. Many sand dams cannot supply a household through the dry season [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3]. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2]. The check-dam and pond findings are secondary citations in reviews, and the Korean result is modelled in a high-income setting [ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. The Indian spring and stream discharge figures come from World Bank completion reports, the lender's own evaluation, measured before and after without untreated comparison sites, for catchment treatment that bundles plantations, trenches, ponds and check dams with water-harvesting structures, so the gain cannot be credited to water harvesting alone [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1, ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. What upstream capture does to water downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows. The measured soil-moisture evidence has its own limits. Tillage alone is not water harvesting: in the Brazilian trial deep ploughing, which is tillage alone, scored as high as the tied furrows, so that treatment does not speak for the practice [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. The Ethiopian basins did not differ from unmulched plots at planting at Ziway or at any stage at Melkassa [ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_2, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_8, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_10, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_12]. Under meteorological drought and dry spells in Kenya, tied ridging without organic inputs was insufficient in soil moisture conservation since there was little or no rainwater to be held in the basins [ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]: structures store rain, they cannot make it. A review found no significant effect of infiltration trenches on soil moisture because only four studies provided sufficient statistical data [ev_soil_water_retention_locat20_1]. The zaï and half-moon results come with compost in the pits, so the moisture gain cannot be credited to the pit alone [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8], the Indian watershed comparison is a project-commissioned study of a package of soil and water conservation structures [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2], and the Brazilian tied-furrow trial ran a single season at a station of the agency that promotes the technology [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. Soil moisture is read as a component of water stress, not water stress itself. Those best-practice arms are bundled: planting pits, basins or ripper-with-ridging (the capture element, which is the practice here) come with reduced tillage and mostly with fertiliser, and tillage alone is not water harvesting [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. The trial-level readings are weaker: the authors find no clear tillage effect on rain water productivity in Kenya, no clear effects of tillage in Ethiopia (where the gains that do show come with fertilised treatments), and only a tendency of improvement in semi-arid Tanzania [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_5, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_4]. The Burkina Faso trial covers a single season, and every conservation arm also received manure, so its gain belongs to the package rather than to the structures alone [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_1]. At Houndé, grass strips with zaï (4.84 against 3.10) were not significantly different from the control, and at Péni neither grass strips with zaï (4.51) nor earth bunds with contour ploughing (4.31) differed significantly from the control (3.53), the authors stating that water was not limiting at Péni, which had more rain than Houndé that season [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_4]. The Sudan comparison ranks treatments without a no-practice value [ev_rain_water_productivity_ngur26_3]. These are compiler and author judgements across groups, direction only, and the review sentence is second-hand; the WOCAT authors also note that some case studies indicate little to no improvement in water use efficiency [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. The FAO and WOCAT group marks are compiler judgements, direction only, and the conservation agriculture group bundles mulch with minimum tillage and rotation [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_4].

Well-level evidence for semi-arid bunds and zaï now sits in the catchment water yield rows. What upstream capture does to water downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows. The zaï and half-moon results come with compost in the pits, so the moisture gain cannot be credited to the pit alone [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8].
